summary: The Dodgers–Yankees rivalry is one of MLB's best-known, between the NL West's Los Angeles Dodgers and the AL East's New York Yankees. The teams have met 11 times in the World Series, more than any other AL–NL pair, with the Yankees winning 8 of them. After the Dodgers moved from Brooklyn to Los Angeles in 1958 the rivalry persisted, and regular season games since 2004 draw sellout crowds, with the Dodgers leading the regular season series 7–6.
one_line: The Dodgers and Yankees have met 11 times in the World Series, the most of any AL–NL pair, and the rivalry endures in regular season play.
key_facts: The Dodgers and Yankees have met 11 times in the World Series, more than any other pair of teams from the American and National Leagues.
The rivalry began in New York City, when the Dodgers played in Brooklyn; the Dodgers moved to Los Angeles in 1958.
Since the 1980s the rivalry has also pitted the two largest cities in the United States.
The Dodgers and Yankees have not met in the World Series since 1981, when the Dodgers won 4–2.
The first meeting was on October 1, 1941 at the original Yankee Stadium in the World Series.
The first regular season meeting was June 18, 2004 at Dodger Stadium, in a 3-game interleague series.
The Dodgers lead the regular season series 7–6, and total meetings number 78 (World Series: 65, regular season: 13).
The latest meeting was September 14, 2016 at Dodger Stadium, a 2–0 Dodgers win.
The Yankees won the 1941, 1947, 1949, 1952, 1953, 1956, 1977 and 1978 World Series against the Dodgers.
The Dodgers won the World Series over the Yankees in 1955 (4–3), 1963 (4–0) and 1981 (4–2).
The largest World Series victory was 12–2 for the Yankees on October 15, 1978; the largest regular season victory was 6–0 for the Dodgers on June 19, 2013.
The Dodgers' longest win streak is 2 (June 19, 2013 – July 30, 2013); the Yankees' is 2 (June 27, 2010 – June 19, 2013).
